messages:
Sara (Support): Heads-up: Acme reports huge drop in vectors/sec for /v1/embeddings since ~09:10 UTC. Tokens/sec looks normal. Customer says nothing changed on their side.
Jonah (Infra): on it — any request ids or sample payloads?
Sara (Support): pasted one request id: req_0a1b2c3d, sample payload size ~1.2KB, dim=1536. They also included a curl that retries on 401s.
Mona (ML): dim 1536 is expected for that model. Do they sometimes send 768-dim vectors? that could force fallback.
Sara (Support): they said ~5% of requests are legacy 768 dims (old client). Could that explain throughput drop?
Leo (Runtime): possibly. Small fraction of wrong-dim requests can break batching: runtime stalls to validate/convert and ends up sending single-request batches. Also if auth retries cause bursts, queue depth oscillates.
Jonah (Infra): pulling metrics: GPU queue depth spiked at 09:12 — queued_slots 120 -> 900 for the vecs pool. Concurrent_batches dropped from 24 -> 4.
thoth-bot: [deploy-bot] noticed auth-middleware rollout at 08:50 UTC; version v2.14.1 -> v2.15.0.
Mona (ML): that rollout included stricter dim-checking on ingress (fast path reject vs convert). If legacy clients now get 401s and retry, that will create many tiny requests hitting queue; combined with dim-rejects causing sync conversions, can thrash KV cache.
Sara (Support): customer logs show many 401 -> immediate retry within 200ms. Sequence snippet: ```HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Retrying...
POST /v1/embeddings 200 OK```
Leo (Runtime): small retries + wrong-dim conversions = increased per-request overhead and less batching. Check tokens/sec vs vectors/sec graphs: tokens steady ~18k/s, vectors fell from 2.1k/s -> 400/s. That ratio drop matches batching collapse.
Jonah (Infra): repro on staging: replayed traffic with 5% 768 dims + 5% 401-retries -> vectors/sec dropped 68% and GPU util lower (40%). Logs show kvcache locks - frequent invalidations.
Mona (ML): root cause hypothesis: auth rollout changed cache-key semantics causing short TTL misses for some API keys. Clients seeing 401, retry quickly. Meanwhile wrong-dim requests cause runtime to take slow-path quantization/reshape, blocking batching windows. Combined effect -> queue depth spike and throughput regression.
Sara (Support): customer asked for immediate mitigation — recommended steps?
Leo (Runtime): short-term mitigations: 1) throttle immediate client retries (introduce small backoff) 2) temporarily revert strict dim-reject policy to accept+convert on ingress 3) pin Acme to a dedicated route so their retries don't contaminate the shared vec pool.
Jonah (Infra): I can pin Acme to dedicated route and raise their route concurrency. Also rolling back auth TTL change for keys issued before 08:50.
Mona (ML): I can adjust runtime to batch across mixed dims by queueing conversion work off the critical path (async convert) so it doesn't block the main batcher. That needs a small patch but can land in few hours.
Sara (Support): I'll tell Acme: 1) we're pinning them and reverting TTLs; 2) ask them to update client (no immediate retry on 401) and ensure they stop sending legacy 768-dim requests or upgrade client; 3) internal follow-ups as listed.
Jonah (Infra): done: pinned route + revert scheduled, deploying now (thx).
thoth-bot: [monitor] created incident INC-5231 and scheduled a postmortem.
Leo (Runtime): quick log snippet from repro: ```kvcache: lock acquired 0.9ms -> held 120ms for conversion; batch_window expired; emitted small batch size=1```
Mona (ML): confirming: if conversion holds kvcache for >50ms it kills throughput. We should instrument conversion latency per-dim and add SLA.
Sara (Support): Acme confirmed vectors/sec recovered to ~90% after pinning/rollback and advised they'd throttle retries. They want postmortem.
Jonah (Infra): marking incident resolved for now, tracking postmortem actions: auth TTL rollback, runtime conversion async patch, and customer-facing doc about client retry/backoff.
Sara (Support): thanks team. I'll follow up with the customer and share postmortem when ready. :white_check_mark:
